consumer: An engine condition/eligibility check asking the yes/no 'does the avatar carry at least 250 charges of water_clean?', evaluated as a computed quantity-threshold predicate over the character's own inventory.
scope: only the character's own carried items, counted by CHARGES (water_clean is count_by_charges), not by item-stack entries; threshold = 250 charges.
decisive_source: The decisive 250-charge routine is NOT shown at the needed reach: src/visitable.cpp::amount_of_internal/has_amount tallies matching ITEM ENTRIES (+1 per item, capped at qty) and returns tally==qty, which is the wrong magnitude for a charge-based item; src/condition.cpp::set_has_item evaluates charges_of(id)>0 || has_amount(id,1), a real engine-condition consumer (class C) but a >=1 PRESENCE check, the wrong threshold. The correct authority is the engine's own charges_of/amount_of charge count over the avatar compared to 250, which is not provided.
divergence: Avatar carries a single canteen holding 300 charges of water_clean (one count_by_charges item entry). True answer is YES (300>=250), but has_amount(water_clean,250) counts item entries and finds 1<250, returning NO; re-deriving from the carried_items JSON snapshot likewise mis-handles charges vs stacks.
